gappers.catalyst: Q3 2026 results out this morning at 6:45 AM ET plus a board-authorized share repurchase of up to $300 million: adjusted revenue rose to $84.4M from $76.5M even as digital-asset sales fell to $32.1B from $41.6B.
headlines: Bullish Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results (Nov 18, 6:45 AM ET) - stocktitan.net
Issuer Token Coalition surges to 12 firms as DRW, Flow Traders, SoFi and Superstate join (Nov 17, 4:05 PM ET) - stocktitan.net

gappers.catalyst_detail: Bullish reported Q3 2026 before the open today (6:45 AM ET, call at 8:30 AM) and the board authorized up to $300M of share repurchases - roughly 9% of a ~$3.4B market cap. The mix is genuinely split: adjusted revenue rose to $84.4M from $76.5M, but digital-asset sales fell to $32.1B from $41.6B, consistent with the company's own October monthly metrics showing volume down to $37.7B from $48.6B in September. Separately, on Nov 17 after the close Bullish and Equiniti added DRW, Flow Traders, SoFi and Superstate to their Issuer Token Coalition, taking it to 12 firms, though participation is explicitly non-binding. Stacey Cunningham, former NYSE Group President, joined as President on Nov 9.
gappers.why: Revenue grew while volumes shrank, which says take-rate expansion rather than volume growth, and the $300M buyback is the real lever: a repurchase authorization worth ~9% of market cap, announced on a stock sitting at its 20-day low after a crypto drawdown, puts a bid under a heavily de-rated float and forces short covering. The move is a buyback-plus-beat squeeze off a washed-out base, not a demand-growth re-rating.
gappers.impact: Reads as a real catalyst rather than a headline spike - a buyback authorization is a durable, dated change in the share count, and the earnings call at 8:30 AM ET can extend or kill the move. But the base is badly broken: price is -13.3% vs its 20-SMA, -30.3% vs its 50-SMA and -32.8% vs its 200-SMA, with RSI14 at 29.9 (oversold). Sector read-through is to the crypto-exchange and digital-asset complex, which is working against it - CoinDesk has bitcoin in its sixth consecutive weekly loss, down 23% from its late-September high, so the parent tape is still falling while this single name gaps up on company news.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The buyback is structural, but the move is a bounce off the 20-day low inside a confirmed downtrend (below the 20-, 50- and 200-SMA) in a sector that appears nowhere in the strategy's late-cycle favored set of Energy, Materials and Financials; a LONG_TERM call needs the crypto tape to stop falling first.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace - the account is flat at $100,000 with 0 of 6 position slots used and 0 of 3 weekly trades spent - so the true cost is one of three weekly trade slots and the attention of today's remaining three scans. On R:R this is the ONLY name of the three that clears the mechanical gate: ATR14 is 8.65% of price, so a 10% stop is 1.16 ATR and a +20% target is 2.31 ATR, meaning 2:1 is actually reachable at a permitted stop distance. It fails the Indicator Canon's long-bias filter instead, trading 32.8% below its 200-SMA, and buying an oversold RSI in a downtrend is the bottom-fishing the rulebook forbids outright. ATR sizing would put it at 545 shares, about $11,500 or 11.5% of equity, inside the 20% cap. Research only, no order.

headlines: PepGen Announces Pricing of $125 Million Public Offering - 25,000,000 shares at $5.00, closing on or about Nov 13 (Nov 11, 10:22 PM ET) - stocktitan.net
PepGen Stock Doubles in One Session - Here's Why (Nov 10) - benzinga.com

gappers.catalyst_detail: There is no PepGen press release dated Nov 17 or 18. The sequence driving today's gap began on Nov 10, when PepGen reported Phase 2 FREEDOM2-DM1 results for its 10 mg/kg cohort showing 46.5% mean splicing correction at Week 13 for PGN-EDODM1 in myotonic dystrophy type 1, and the stock doubled in a session. Management immediately monetized the move: a $125M offering launched the same afternoon and priced on Nov 11 at $5.00 for 25,000,000 shares, closing Nov 13, with a 30-day underwriter option on 3.75M more. Q3 showed a $19.4M net loss and $104.8M of cash at Sept 30, so the raise roughly doubles the cash runway. Guggenheim raised its target to $15 on Nov 13 and BofA upgraded to Neutral. The next hard catalyst is the fully enrolled 12.5 mg/kg cohort, guided to the first half of 2027.
gappers.why: The mechanism is the offering overhang, not news. Pricing 25M new shares at $5.00 handed every buyer a reference price, the stock broke below it, and the subsequent slide (-7.25% on Nov 14, down to $3.86 by Nov 17) took it ~23% under the deal price. Today's +7% is a dilution-flush snapback off that low by traders treating sub-$4 as a discount to the $5.00 institutions just paid, with no new information behind it.
gappers.impact: Reads as a one-day bounce likely to mean-revert. Prior-session volume of 5.6M against an IEX 20-day average of 251k confirms the name is still being churned by post-deal rotation rather than accumulated, and the chart is an unresolved spike: a 20-day range of $2.23 to $6.38 on a $4.15 price. Decisively, the next clinical readout is a 2027 event, so there is nothing scheduled to sustain a move for months, while the 3.75M-share underwriter option stays live as fresh supply. Read-through is limited - this is single-asset DM1 biotech risk with no sector complex moving alongside it.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The Phase 2 data is structural but is already priced and then diluted, and with the next cohort not reading out until H1 2027 there is no durable thesis to carry; the strategy's late-cycle favored sectors do not include speculative clinical-stage biotech.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace (flat account, 0 of 6 slots, 0 of 3 weekly trades), so the cost is one weekly slot. Notably PEPG is the ONLY name in today's list that PASSES the 200-SMA long-bias filter, trading +42.1% above it, with RSI14 at a neutral 58.2 - the cleanest trend structure of the three. It fails on R:R instead, and badly: ATR14 is 15.24% of price, so a 10% stop is just 0.66 ATR and a +20% target only 1.31 ATR, meaning a permitted stop sits well inside a single average day's range and would fire on noise before the thesis resolved. gappers.catalyst: No company news - AI-infrastructure sympathy bounce after NVIDIA reported Q3 FY2027 results after the close on Nov 17 and beat, lifting the neocloud complex off its lows.
headlines: NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Third Quarter Fiscal 2027 (Nov 17, after close) - quantisnow.com
Nebius Rises 10% After Nvidia Earnings Beat (Nov 17, after hours) - timothysykes.com
Nebius Revenue Jumps to $980.8 Million, but Capacity Delays Weigh (Nov 12) - stockinvest.us
Nebius secures $3.5 billion senior secured financing facility from Citi (Oct 22) - stocktitan.net
gappers.catalyst_detail: No Nebius release is dated Nov 17 or 18; the driver is external. NVIDIA reported Q3 fiscal 2027 after the close on Nov 17 and beat, with the earnings call at 7:00 PM ET, and the Nvidia-backed AI-cloud complex rallied with it - Nebius traded up about 10% in the after-hours session. That bounce is off a deep hole of Nebius's own making. Q3, reported Nov 12, actually beat: revenue $980.8M, up 571% year over year, with operating income turning positive. The market traded the guidance instead - the top end of FY26 revenue guidance was cut, data-centre capacity delays were flagged, and capex was raised toward ~$45B - and the stock fell 16.8% that day and kept sliding, roughly 42% below its 20-day high. Baird cut its target from $340 to $200 and BofA to $265, and a Reddit compilation of Nov 13-16 revisions shows analysts still cutting into this week.
gappers.why: This is borrowed momentum, not repaired fundamentals. Nebius is the highest-beta listed expression of Nvidia GPU demand, so an NVDA beat mechanically lifts it regardless of its own capacity-delay problem. Nothing in the move addresses the two things that broke the stock six sessions ago - the guidance cut and the ~$45B capex requirement - so the bid is sector beta reclaiming an oversold level.
gappers.impact: Most likely to mean-revert of the three, because the catalyst is not its own and the de-rate is sustained rather than a spike: price is -22.2% vs its 20-SMA, -40.5% vs its 50-SMA and -37.3% vs its 200-SMA, with RSI14 at 33.8. Prior-session volume of 31.8M is heavy but the IEX ratio of 1.10x average shows no accumulation surge behind this particular bounce. Sector read-through is the key risk: CRWV and the rest of the neocloud complex are moving on exactly the same NVDA print, so taking NBIS and any peer would be one macro trade expressed twice - precisely what corr-gate.mjs exists to block.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: A peer's earnings beat is not a durable thesis for this name, the guidance reset that caused the selloff is structurally bearish and unaddressed, and analyst targets were still being cut through Nov 16.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace (flat account, 0 of 6 slots, 0 of 3 weekly trades), so the cost is one weekly slot spent on the worst-trending name in the list. It is the only one of the three failing BOTH gates: ATR14 is 15.89% of price, so a 10% stop is 0.63 ATR - under two-thirds of an average day's range and near-certain to fire on noise - while a +20% target is only 1.26 ATR, so 2:1 is unreachable at any permitted stop; and at -37.3% vs its 200-SMA the long-bias filter fails outright. It would also stack AI-capex beta that today's tape is driving across the whole neocloud group. Strictly dominated within today's own list: BLSH offers better R:R shape and PEPG a better trend. ATR sizing would be 55 shares, about $6,195 or 6.2% of equity. Research only, no order.
